frameworks.name: 10-Stage Scaling Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A predictable progression from zero to 100M+ revenue with eight functions per stage, identifying constraints, symptoms, and graduation steps repeated across software, physical products, services, and brick-and-mortar.

claims.text: A service business can mathematically reach $12M annual revenue at current unit economics without any changes to pricing, sales motion, or strategy. Alex Hormozi calculated this from the agency's metrics: $5,000 average monthly contract value, 5% monthly churn, 10 units sold monthly yields $1M LTV × 10 units = $1M monthly run rate = $12M annually. The agency is currently at $7M, so $5M in additional revenue is projected to arrive automatically.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service business with recurring monthly contracts
$5k price point and 5% monthly churn rate
claims.mechanism: Customer lifetime value multiplied by monthly sales volume determines revenue ceiling at stable unit economics.

numbers.axis: Annual revenue projection by service business LTV formula

bounded_by: Does not apply without stable monthly recurring pricing

claims.text: Service business gross margin must target 80%, not industry-average 50%. Alex Hormozi reframes industry benchmarks as meaningless because they average poor performers. The only reason to measure against average is to anchor yourself to lower standards. With AI and nearshoring, a service agency has no excuse to operate below 80% gross margin.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service business with scalable delivery operations
AI and nearshoring available as cost levers
claims.mechanism: Lower margins reduce reinvestment velocity; 80% margin compounds faster than 50% margin at equivalent revenue scale.
bounded_by: Does not apply to commodity retail where margins are naturally thin
Assumes ability to offshore and automate delivery operations

claims.text: The primary barrier preventing the agency owner from selling their company for $20M is not pricing or sales motion but operational margin. The owner currently has 13% EBITDA and needs margin expansion. If the business reaches $12M revenue with 50% gross margin, but improves operational flow to yield 6M in operating margin (improving EBITDA), it becomes saleable at $20M valuation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Exit valuations correlate with EBITDA multiple; improving operational efficiency directly increases buyer perception of quality and cash flow stability.

claims.text: Nearly 80% of work in a service delivery operation like SEO/web/PPC is automatable today with AI, not tomorrow. This is not a threat but an opportunity. The agency that automates its delivery can undercut competitors who lag behind and improve margins simultaneously. By becoming an AI-integrated generation (AIG) business, the agency captures market risk as market advantage.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: SEO, web, and PPC service delivery
AI agents and automation tools (ChatGPT, Make.com) available and adopted
claims.mechanism: Automating repetitive delivery tasks frees labor for higher-value account management and reduces cost-of-goods-sold, improving gross margin and competitive positioning simultaneously.

numbers.axis: Percentage of service delivery work automatable by AI

bounded_by: Account management and client relationship remain human-driven
Assumes continuous skill development in AI/automation tools

claims.text: Nearshoring (building a nearshore operations team) combined with AI automation is the path to improve service business margins from 50% to 80%. The agency is currently at first-five employees; adding 10 more through nearshore over three months is feasible and will unlock the operational capacity needed to handle the $5M incremental revenue coming from natural growth.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Nearshore hiring reduces labor cost and improves utilization, allowing one manager to oversee more delivery capacity per unit employee cost.
bounded_by: Quality-of-hire in nearshore markets can vary; requires active management
Assumes 3-month ramp time is achievable for 10 new hires

claims.text: The stated 5% monthly churn in a $5k-per-month service business is high and indicates pricing risk or delivery quality issues. Alex Hormozi flags this as a data point requiring diagnosis, though the agency owner's revenue run rate suggests the churn is manageable relative to overall growth.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: High-touch B2B service businesses at $5k/month price point
claims.mechanism: Churn reduces LTV; at 5% monthly, customers have average tenure of 20 months, reducing lifetime value and requiring faster sales velocity to maintain growth.

numbers.axis: Monthly churn rate and implied customer lifetime in months

bounded_by: Churn benchmark varies by vertical and contract structure

examples.text: The agency owner is selling SEO, websites, and PPC to roofing, HVAC, and home-services companies. At $5,000 average monthly recurring revenue, 5% monthly churn, and 10 units sold per month, the business naturally scales to $12M annual revenue. The owner wants to reach $14M and sell the company for $20M. The constraint is not demand or pricing but EBITDA margin (currently 13%) and operational capacity (currently 5 employees, expanding to 15 via nearshoring).

Alex Hormozi challenges the owner's belief that 80% margins are unachievable in an SEO/web/PPC business. He notes that American industry averages are meaningless (they reflect poor average performers), and that with AI and nearshoring, no reason exists to accept 50% gross margin. He shows multiple examples of SEO agencies running 50%+ net margins, and with automation, the owner's agency should exceed 80%.

practices.text: Get up to speed on AI agents and automation tools like Make.com (successor to Zapier automations). Spend time building competency in ChatGPT and LLM-based agents so you can identify which 80% of your delivery work can be automated.

Track gross margin as the primary operational metric, not industry averages. Compare your performance against best-in-class competitors and your own potential, not against the average which is anchored to poor performers.

Frame AI automation as a market advantage and risk-capture opportunity, not as a threat. The agency that automates earliest will win margin and market share from competitors who remain labor-dependent.
